---
title: Enforce constraints with unique indexes
description: Having a unique index on your hypertable simplifies lookup, speeds up aggregation, and makes JOINs more efficient. Learn to create a unique index and what the related limitations are.
products: [cloud, self_hosted]
keywords: [hypertables, unique indexes, primary keys]
---

import * as C from "@constants";
import { Callout } from "@stainless-api/docs/components";
import { NumberedList, NumberedItem } from "@components/NumberedList";
import CreateHypertablePolicyNote from "../../../../partials/_create-hypertable-columnstore-policy-note.mdx";

You use unique indexes on a {C.HYPERTABLE} to enforce [constraints](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-constraints.html). If you have a primary key,
you have a unique index. In {C.PG}, a primary key is a unique index with a `NOT NULL` constraint.

You do not need to have a unique index on your {C.HYPERTABLE}s. When you create a unique index,
it must contain all the partitioning columns of the {C.HYPERTABLE}.

## Create a {C.HYPERTABLE} and add unique indexes

To create a unique index on a {C.HYPERTABLE}:

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title="Determine the partitioning columns">

Before you create a unique index, you need to determine which unique indexes are
allowed on your {C.HYPERTABLE}. Begin by identifying your partitioning columns.

{C.TIMESCALE_DB} traditionally uses the following columns to partition {C.HYPERTABLE}s:

*   The `time` column used to create the {C.HYPERTABLE}. Every {C.TIMESCALE_DB} {C.HYPERTABLE}
    is partitioned by time.
*   Any space-partitioning columns. Space partitions are optional and not
    included in every {C.HYPERTABLE}.

</NumberedItem>
<NumberedItem title={`Create a ${C.HYPERTABLE}`}>

Create a [{C.HYPERTABLE}](/learn/hypertables/understand-hypertables) for your time-series data using [CREATE TABLE](/reference/timescaledb/hypertables/create_table).
For [efficient queries](/build/performance-optimization/secondary-indexes) on data in the {C.COLUMNSTORE}, remember to `segmentby` the column you will
use most often to filter your data. For example:

```sql
CREATE TABLE hypertable_example(
  time TIMESTAMPTZ,
  user_id BIGINT,
  device_id BIGINT,
  value FLOAT
) WITH (
  tsdb.hypertable,
  tsdb.segmentby = 'device_id',
  tsdb.orderby = 'time DESC'
);
```

<CreateHypertablePolicyNote />

</NumberedItem>
<NumberedItem title={`Create a unique index on the ${C.HYPERTABLE}`}>

When you create a unique index on a {C.HYPERTABLE}, it must contain all the partitioning columns. It may contain
other columns as well, and they may be arranged in any order. You cannot create a unique index without `time`,
because `time` is a partitioning column.

For example:

- Create a unique index on `time` and `device_id` with a call to `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX`:

   ```sql
   CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_deviceid_time
     ON hypertable_example(device_id, time);
   ```

- Create a unique index on `time`, `user_id`, and `device_id`.

  `device_id` is not a partitioning column, but this still works:

   ```sql
   CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_userid_deviceid_time
     ON hypertable_example(user_id, device_id, time);
   ```

<Callout variant="note">
This restriction is necessary to guarantee global uniqueness in the index.
</Callout>

</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

## Create a {C.HYPERTABLE} from an existing table with unique indexes

If you create a unique index on a table before turning it into a {C.HYPERTABLE}, the
same restrictions apply in reverse. You can only partition the table by columns
in your unique index.

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title="Create a relational table">

```sql
CREATE TABLE another_hypertable_example(
  time TIMESTAMPTZ,
  user_id BIGINT,
  device_id BIGINT,
  value FLOAT
);
```

</NumberedItem>
<NumberedItem title="Create a unique index on the table">

For example, on `device_id` and `time`:

```sql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_deviceid_time
  ON another_hypertable_example(device_id, time);
```

</NumberedItem>
<NumberedItem title={`Turn the table into a partitioned ${C.HYPERTABLE}`}>

- On `time` alone:

   ```sql
   SELECT * from create_hypertable('another_hypertable_example', by_range('time'));
   ```

- On `time` and `device_id`:

   ```sql
   SELECT * FROM create_hypertable('another_hypertable_example', by_range('time'));
   SELECT * FROM add_dimension('another_hypertable_example', by_hash('device_id', 4));
   ```

You get an error if you try to turn the relational table into a {C.HYPERTABLE} partitioned by `time` and `user_id`.
This is because `user_id` is not part of the `UNIQUE INDEX`. To fix the error, add `user_id` to your unique index.

</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>
